title: "Data"
---

## Data root

Raw data, except for ROSE, lives in the
[HuggingFace sepsis collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/cmatkhan/sepsis-transcriptomics) (ROSE comes from dbGaP).
Download this collection to a local directory, eg `~/projects/sepsis_transcriptomics_collection`.
The dataset configs give paths relative to that local root and is set by the 
environmental variable `SEPSIS_DATA_ROOT` environmental variable.

## Dataset configs

Each `config/<dataset>_config.yml` describes where its data is,
how to build it, and each configured latent factor method's parameter grid.
Subsets analysed separately (e.g. one timepoint) are separate configs, each
with its own `dataset.id`; there's no "several matrices in one config".
[config/dataset_metadata.example.yml](https://github.com/cmatKhan/sepsis_latent_factor_eda/blob/main/config/dataset_metadata.example.yml)
is a fully commented template. Configs are read and validated by
`read_dataset_metadata()` / `validate_dataset_metadata()` (`R/lib/metadata.R`).

### Adding a dataset

A dataset is three parquet files in one directory under the data root, a config,
and a line in `config/pipeline.yml`. The files are named by the config's
`*_path` keys (conventionally `<dataset>/expression.parquet`,
`feature_metadata.parquet` and `sample_metadata.parquet`).
Extra columns are ignored.

| File | One row per | Columns the config names |
|---|---|---|
| `expression.parquet` | feature × sample (long format) | `feature_id_col`, `sample_id_col`, `value_col`. Defaults `feature_id`, `sample_id`, `value`; existing configs use `GeneID` or `IlluminaID` for the feature column. Counts for RNA-seq, log-scale values for arrays: the pipeline normalizes nothing by itself. |
| `feature_metadata.parquet` | feature | `feature_id_col`: unique, and the same ids as the expression file's features. `ensembl_col`: Ensembl gene id (a `;`-separated list takes its first gene); every comparison across datasets goes through it. `symbol_col`: gene symbol; display only, except that arrays with a `design:` block are collapsed to one probe per symbol. |
| `sample_metadata.parquet` | sample | `sample_id_col`: the same ids as the expression file's samples. Plus every column a `design:` block names (subject, time, group, covariates), and `subject_id_col` if you set it. |

The sample metadata file is optional: without it (e.g. SHIP-TREND) the dataset gets
factor fits but no design, variance or composition analysis.

1. Put the three files under `<data root>/<dataset>/`.
2. Write `config/<dataset>_config.yml`, starting from `config/dataset_metadata.example.yml`: the
   three paths (relative to the data root), the column names above, a `methods:` block, usually
   a `preprocessing_script` ([Building a matrix](#building-a-matrix)), and a `design:` block
   if you want the repeated-measures analysis ([below](#the-design-block)).
3. Add its `dataset.id` to `datasets:` in `config/pipeline.yml`.
4. Run the pipeline. Only the new dataset's targets are built.
5. Optionally record it in [Datasets](datasets.qmd): a section whose heading is the dataset id
   (anchor `{#<lowercase id>}`). The app's Design and model tab links to that section for datasets
   whose config says `hf_collection: "cmatkhan/Sepsis transcriptomics"`; nothing in the pipeline
   reads it.

File names needn't match ids (`ANEMONES_day1_config.yml` declares `ANEMONES_DAY1`); the
pipeline finds a config by its declared `dataset.id`.

Every key of the `dataset:`, `design:` and `methods:` blocks is documented in the comments of
the example config; each method's keys are also in [Methods](methods.qmd). The notes below
cover the parts that are easy to miss.

### The `design:` block

Optional. A dataset with one gets the repeated-measures analysis ([Methods](methods.qmd)).
`group_at_first_time: true` is for a group that changes over time (GSE13904's "SIRS
resolved"): every sample takes its subject's first-timepoint group. Per-timepoint subsets
have no `design:` block: their factors are described with their parent's design
(`variance_parent()`, `R/targets/variance.R`).

**Composition markers.** `config/composition_markers.yml` lists the neutrophil and
lymphocyte marker genes behind the per-sample composition scores
(`analyze_composition()`, `R/targets/composition.R`). Editing it reruns only the
composition targets and what reads them.

### YAML keys that are booleans

R's `yaml` package reads an **unquoted** key that is a YAML 1.1 boolean token -- `y`, `n`,
`yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `true`, `false`, in any capitalization -- as `TRUE`/`FALSE`, not
the string you wrote. A method argument literally named `n` silently becomes the key
`FALSE`. `read_dataset_metadata()` errors on a `TRUE`/`FALSE` key under `methods:`; quote
such keys (`"n": [...]`).

## Building a matrix

The pipeline never assumes a normalization or metadata values. `load_input_matrix()`
(`R/lib/matrices.R`) builds the matrix one of three ways, first match wins:

| # | Config | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dataset.matrix_path` | reads that RDS matrix as-is |
| 2 | `dataset.preprocessing_script` | runs your script against the raw parquet trio |
| 3 | neither | pivots `expression_path` wide -- no normalization, no filtering |

Every current dataset uses a preprocessing script (`R/preprocessing/<dataset>_preprocessing.R`),
run by `run_preprocessing_script()` (`R/lib/matrices.R`).
The result must be a plain matrix with row names = feature ids and column names = sample ids.
Any sample or gene filtering belongs in the script (or the prebuilt matrix).

### Preprocessing-script contract

The script is `source()`d with these variables already defined:

| Variable | From |
|---|---|
| `expression_path`, `sample_metadata_path`, `feature_metadata_path` | `dataset.*_path` |
| `sample_id_col`, `feature_id_col`, `value_col`, `ensembl_col` | `dataset.*_col` |
| `tmp_dir` | a directory created for this run |

It must write its feature × sample matrix to `file.path(tmp_dir, "matrix.rds")`. To also run
it by hand, guard on `tmp_dir`, which only exists when the pipeline sources the script:

```r
framework_run <- exists("tmp_dir", inherits = FALSE)
if (!framework_run) {
  expression_path <- "~/local/path/to/expression.parquet"   # ... etc.
}
# ... your logic ...
if (framework_run) saveRDS(final_mat, file.path(tmp_dir, "matrix.rds"))
```

The one transform the pipeline applies itself is the non-negativity shift NMF and CoGAPS
need (`shift_nonneg()`, the `mat_nn_<dataset>` target): an algorithm requirement, not a
normalization choice.

## Dataset families

`config/dataset_families.yml` lists which datasets are timepoints or subsets of the same
cohort (e.g. `ANEMONES` and `ANEMONES_DAY1`...`ANEMONES_DISCHARGE`). It decides two things:

- **projectR intercept:** projections within a family leave out the intercept; projections
  across families include it.
- **Gene-space agreement** is computed between datasets in the same family only.

Families are listed explicitly, not inferred from dataset-id naming.

## Gene identifiers across datasets

Each dataset's matrix keeps its platform's own feature ids (Illumina/Affymetrix probes,
Entrez ids, versioned Ensembl ids). Anything that compares datasets or gene sets -- enrichment
and projectR -- first remaps row names to **version-stripped Ensembl gene ids**
(`ENSG00000001234.2` → `ENSG00000001234`) with `build_ensembl_map()`/`remap_to_ensembl()`
(`R/lib/ingest/symbol_mapping.R`), using `dataset.ensembl_col`; a `;`-separated multi-gene
entry takes its first gene. The map (`ensembl_map_<dataset>`) is built once per dataset from
its feature metadata and its matrix, and is one-to-one: where several of the matrix's probes map
to one gene, only the one with the highest mean expression across the dataset's samples is
kept. A gene is then the same probe in the matrix, in every fit's loadings and in every gene
list, and converting is a rename. (Before 2026-10-15 duplicates were collapsed separately in
each matrix, taking each column's largest |value|, which could mix probes across samples and
across factors; 684 of the 35 matrices' 257,544 rows were in such groups, mostly ANEMONES and
GSE95233.) ANEMONES maps poorly: only about 4,200 of its 8,000 rows have an Ensembl id, so the
rest take no part in cross-dataset comparisons.

Gene **symbols** (`build_symbol_map()`, `dataset.symbol_col`) are for display only, never for
matching: symbols are ambiguous and renamed across annotation releases.

A dataset with a missing or wrong `ensembl_col` keeps its native ids, so it matches almost
nothing in other datasets. That shows up not as an error but as near-zero `n_genes_matched`
in `projections` (projectR logs "0 row names matched").

## Which datasets are built

`config/pipeline.yml` lists the 35 datasets the pipeline builds: 12 full datasets (11 with a
`design:` block; SHIP-TREND has no sample metadata) and 23 per-timepoint subsets. One config
is left out:

| Dataset | Why |
|---|---|
| `gains` | `R/preprocessing/gains_preprocessing.R` is an unfinished stub: it reads the four sub-cohort expression files (E-MTAB-4421/4451/5273/5274) but never builds a matrix. Whether to pool the four accessions is still undecided. |

SHIP-TREND (991 healthy samples) has no sample metadata (its phenotype data is
access-restricted): it gets factor fits but no design, variance or composition analysis.
